description: Visualizing Completion of Coastal Projects Reassures Stakeholders is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Maryland Department of Natural Resources | CoastSmart Council; NOAA Office for Coastal Management; USDA National Agroforestry Center. Shoreline property owners weren't sure how changes they needed to make to adapt to rising sea level would look. Maryland Department of Natural Resources staff found a way to create visualizations illustrating the likely visual impact of living shorelines. Coverage: Maryland (2014). The toolkit gives Maryland as the location, 2014 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

In response, some property owners along Maryland's shore built "hard" structural solutions to hold their land in place.
